summary: The attested construction has leban 'our heart' as grammatical subject and aʕlayye as ʕal-marked personal stimulus. The human experiencers are represented by the possessor of the heart, not a verbal l-suffix.
Unprefixed maḥən follows kofoyəš; the ko- belongs to the preceding verb, so it does not justify a new ko-Preterit box for ḥyn.
The inherited cow/calf example has the animal as subject rather than an overt heart noun. Both existing examples are retained without a new participant-based sense or an unproven affective split.
No new stem, form, idiom, numbered sense or correction is warranted by this duplicate attestation.

Does the inherited cow/calf example express the same longing as 73/203 or a broader maternal attachment? Confirm before broadening the gloss beyond sehnen. Are heart subjects preferred or optional for human experiencers?
Correct the misspelled English word compassion
rationale: The last character is Cyrillic т; the English expression is “to have compassion, pity”.
